title: FIFO Queues are All You Need for Cache Eviction (S3-FIFO)
one_line: A cache eviction algorithm built from three static FIFO queues (a 10% probationary queue S, a 90% main queue M with 2-bit-clock reinsertion, and a ghost queue G) that uses quick demotion of one-hit wonders to beat LRU-based state-of-the-art on miss ratio while remaining lock-free and scalable.

repo.evidence: The paper's Availability section (paper.txt p.14, lines 2013-2017) states 'The code and data used in this work are open-sourced at https://github.com/TheSys-lab/sosp23-s3fifo', which is the repo cloned here (Thesys-lab/sosp23-s3fifo). The SOSP'23 artifact-evaluation results page (https://sysartifacts.github.io/sosp2023/results) lists the same URL for this paper. repo/README.md carries the paper's abstract, its BibTeX entry and a CMU copyright notice.
repo.badge_evidence: https://sysartifacts.github.io/sosp2023/results lists 'FIFO Queues are All You Need for Cache Eviction' with Artifacts Available (v1.1), Artifacts Evaluated - Functional (v1.1) and Results Reproduced (v1.1), artifact URL https://github.com/Thesys-lab/sosp23-s3fifo. (ACM DL page returns 403 from this sandbox, so the AE results page is the source.)

H1_open_repo.evidence: Repo is the official artifact (see repo.evidence) and contains the real system, not a placeholder: libCacheSim/libCacheSim/cache/eviction/S3FIFO.c (526 lines of C implementing Algorithm 1 - S3FIFO_evict_fifo at l.310, S3FIFO_evict_main with the 2-bit clock at l.362/386), S3FIFOd.c (the adaptive variant of paper 6.2), 12 baseline policies under libCacheSim/libCacheSim/cache/eviction/, the flash experiment driver libCacheSim/libCacheSim/bin/SOSP23/flash/flash.cpp, a 433-line artifact recipe doc/AE.md, and pre-computed per-trace results under result/cachesim/, result/cachesim_fifo/ and result/demotion/.

H2_no_root.evidence: Nothing in the simulator path needs privilege. The sudo hits are (a) doc/AE.md:8 and libCacheSim/scripts/install_dependency.sh:4-5, an apt convenience script that is replaceable by 'conda install -c conda-forge glib zstd' because libCacheSim/cmake/Modules/FindGLib.cmake:30-36 resolves GLib through pkg-config and CMakeLists.txt:152 does the same for ZSTD; tcmalloc is optional (CMakeLists.txt:167-175 only prints a warning); xgboost/LightGBM are only needed for ENABLE_GLCACHE/ENABLE_LRB which default OFF (CMakeLists.txt:20,23). (b) libCacheSim/CMakeLists.txt:17 and libCacheSim/doc/performance.md:13 are *commented* transparent-hugepage tuning; the code only issues an unprivileged madvise(..., MADV_HUGEPAGE) whose return value is ignored (libCacheSim/libCacheSim/traceReader/reader.c:128-134), and -DUSE_HUGEPAGE=OFF exists (CMakeLists.txt:18). libCacheSim/dockerfile is optional and its steps are the same apt list. No kernel module, eBPF, perf counter, KVM or /proc/sys write anywhere. One exception, out of scope for the simulation-side work: doc/AE.md:231 'bash turboboost.sh disable' for the CacheLib throughput figure (Fig. 8) would need root.

H3_hardware_fit.evidence: CPU-only, single-node, no GPU, no CUDA. Each simulation is a single-threaded C process; libCacheSim/libCacheSim/bin/cachesim/cli_parser.c:99-104,206 shows --num-thread only parallelises independent (algorithm, cache-size) runs, so 16 cores/32 threads maps well and the paper's own scalability claim was measured at 16 threads (Fig. 8, p.10). RAM: simulations hold at most ~10% of a trace's objects at tens of bytes of metadata each, far inside 125 GiB (doc/AE.md:46 documents how to cut parallelism if DRAM is tight). The paper's full 10^6 core-hour / 6594-trace sweep is not reproducible here, but the per-dataset claim of Fig. 7 is reproducible dataset-by-dataset and the repo ships the per-trace ground truth to diff against. distributedComputation/ (CloudLab, up to 100 nodes) is optional tooling, not part of the algorithm.

H4_obtainable_deps_data.evidence: Deps are glib-2.0 + zstd (+ optional tcmalloc) for the C build and numpy + matplotlib (requirements.txt) for plots, plus scikit-learn + lru-dict for the optional Flashield baseline (doc/AE.md:303) - all conda/pip installable in user space. Data: I fetched the index at https://ftp.pdl.cmu.edu/pub/datasets/twemcacheWorkload/cacheDatasets/ (linked from README.md:69 and doc/AE.md:22) and it is a live open directory with 12 dataset folders (alibabaBlock, cloudphysics, fiu, metaCDN, metaKV, metaStorage, msr, systor, tencentBlock, tencentPhoto, twitter, wiki). The 3 proprietary datasets of Table 1 (CDN 1, CDN 2, Social Network 1) are not downloadable, exactly as the paper states, but the repo ships their computed results (result/cachesim/CDN1|CDN2|SocialNetwork1/) and the headline claim survives on the open subset. Constraint to manage, not a blocker: doc/AE.md:44 says the full corpus is ~2 TB compressed vs ~257 GB free, so a named subset must be chosen.

reproduce.target: Figure 7a (p.10), the MSR / FIU / Systor rows: 'S3-FIFO has the lowest mean miss-ratio reduction from FIFO on most datasets' at the large cache size (10% of trace footprint). Secondary, near-free: Table 2 (p.11) MSR blocks - exact S3-FIFO and W-TinyLFU miss ratios at S in {0.01..0.40}, with literal command lines at doc/AE.md:323-341.
reproduce.scale_down: Download only the msr/, fiu/ and systor/ folders from the PDL FTP (tens of GB compressed; traces are read zstd-compressed so no decompression needed) instead of the full ~2 TB corpus. Run './libCacheSim/_build/bin/cachesim <trace> oracleGeneral FIFO,LRU,Clock,ARC,LIRS,TinyLFU,2Q,SLRU,S3FIFO 0 --ignore-obj-size 1 --num-thread 8' per trace, matching the 8 cache-size fractions used in result/cachesim/. Cap parallelism at ~8 concurrent runs to stay inside RAM. If Systor (3.7 B requests) is still too large, add --sample-ratio 0.1 (spatial sampling, libCacheSim/libCacheSim/traceReader/sampling/spatial.c) and disclose it - absolute miss ratios shift slightly but the cross-algorithm ordering that Fig. 7 claims is preserved. Keep the shipped result dirs for the other 11 datasets so scripts/libCacheSim/plot_miss_ratio.py (which raises RuntimeError if any of the 14 dirs is empty, l.73-75) still runs.
reproduce.effort: 2-3 person-days + ~20-60 CPU-core-hours (no GPU); peak ~60 GB disk, <32 GB RAM at 8-way parallelism
reproduce.rationale: Build is a plain cmake+make against glib and zstd with no version pins to fight (libCacheSim/scripts/install_libcachesim.sh), and the only apt step is substitutable with conda via pkg-config. Evaluation scripts exist specifically for this figure (scripts/libCacheSim/plot_miss_ratio.py) and the repo ships per-trace ground truth (e.g. result/cachesim/MSR/hm_0.IQI.bin.txt, one line per algorithm x size with 4-decimal miss ratios) so success is an unambiguous numeric diff against a deterministic simulator. The artifact holds a SOSP'23 'Results Reproduced' badge. The workload fits the machine at paper scale for these three datasets. One concrete gotcha: libCacheSim/CMakeLists.txt:1 is cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.2), which the system CMake 3.25.1 accepts but the 'pip install cmake' 4.x route rejects - use the system cmake or bump line 1. Not reproducible here: Fig. 8 (external Thesys-lab/cachelib-sosp23 repo, heavy CacheLib build, root needed for turboboost.sh) and the full 6594-trace sweep.

addons.name: Size-aware S3-FIFO (S3FIFO-sz)
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that making S3-FIFO's S-to-M promotion decision size-aware - promoting on benefit-per-byte rather than a raw freq>=2 threshold, and sizing S in bytes rather than objects - reduces byte miss ratio by at least 5% on heavy-tailed object workloads (Wikimedia CDN, Tencent Photo, Meta CDN) with no more than a 1% request-miss-ratio regression, compared with stock S3-FIFO.
addons.mechanism: Replace the scalar test in S3FIFO_evict_fifo (S3FIFO.c:324, 'obj_to_evict->S3FIFO.freq >= params->move_to_main_threshold') with a score freq/size^alpha compared against a running quantile maintained in a 256-bucket log-size histogram that is updated on each promotion (O(1) per eviction, no per-object pointers, so the lock-free argument survives). Leave the ghost-hit fast path to M untouched so scan resistance is preserved. Add 'alpha' and 'size-aware' keys to S3FIFO_parse_params (S3FIFO.c:486) and register the variant in the cachesim dispatch table. Evaluate with --ignore-obj-size 0 using the byte-miss-ratio column cachesim already prints.
addons.motivating_evidence: Paper 5.1 (p.7): 'we ignore object size in the simulator because most production systems use slab storage for memory management ... However, we remark that supporting object size is non-trivial for systems that do not use slab-based memory management.' Paper 5.2 (p.10) relegates byte miss ratio to one paragraph, 'not shown due to space limit', even though 2.1 (p.2) says CDNs use byte miss ratio as their primary bandwidth metric. In code, size handling is currently a blunt rejection: S3FIFO_can_insert (S3FIFO.c:468) drops any object larger than S, and S3FIFO_insert (l.274) silently returns NULL for such objects.
addons.feasibility_rationale: About 300 LOC confined to one eviction module plus two registration lines. The harness (cachesim), the metric (byte miss ratio is already computed and printed) and the traces (wiki, tencentPhoto, metaCDN are all on the open PDL FTP) already exist. Each trace is a few CPU-hours on one core, and 16 cores are available. Clearly within reach of 2-4 students in 10 weeks.
addons.research_value_rationale: It closes a simplifying assumption the authors themselves flag, and a negative result would be a useful robustness statement about S3-FIFO on CDN workloads. But size-aware caching is a well-trodden area (GDSF, AdaptSize, LHD) and recent work already reports S3-FIFO being weak on large-object traces, so a reviewer would call the direction expected rather than surprising.

scoop_check.details: Queries: 'size-aware S3-FIFO byte miss ratio CDN variable object size eviction improvement libCacheSim'; 'S3-FIFO size-aware variable object size cache eviction follow-up 2025'. Closest work: 3L-Cache (FAST '25, https://www.usenix.org/system/files/fast25-zhou-wenbin.pdf), a learned size-aware CDN eviction policy that uses S3-FIFO as a baseline; and SCION (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01055), which selects among size-aware experts (GDSF, LHD) plus S3-FIFO per workload and reports beating S3-FIFO on large-object traces. Neither makes S3-FIFO itself size-aware - both route around it - so the specific mechanism is unclaimed, but the headline finding that S3-FIFO is weak on large-object CDN traces is already public.

addons.name: Sampled-shadow-simulation adaptive S sizing (S3FIFO-mini)
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that choosing S3-FIFO's small-queue ratio online from a bank of spatially-sampled miniature shadow simulations (1/100-scale S3-FIFO instances at S in {1,2,5,10,20,40}%) matches static S=10% on the bulk of traces and recovers most of the loss on the tail where 10% is far from optimal, beating the paper's own S3-FIFO-d on both mean and P10 miss-ratio reduction across the open datasets.
addons.mechanism: libCacheSim already ships spatial sampling (traceReader/sampling/spatial.c, exposed as --sample-ratio via cli_parser.c:286-289). Build a new eviction module that owns k shadow S3-FIFO caches, each sized sample_ratio * cache_size and fed only the requests whose object-ID hash falls in the sample (one hash test in find, off the hot path for the real cache). Every W requests, pick the shadow with the lowest windowed miss ratio and move the real S/M boundary toward its ratio by a bounded step. The real data path is untouched, so the lock-free/scalability argument survives. Compare against static S3FIFO.c and marginal-hit S3FIFOd.c on the trace set behind Fig. 11.
addons.motivating_evidence: Paper 6.2 (pp.12-13) is a page-long admission of failure: 'we compare S3-FIFO-d and S3-FIFO ... and find that S3-FIFO is better than S3-FIFO-d on most traces except the 2% traces at the tail'; 'tuning for a few traces is easy, but obtaining good results across traces is very challenging'; 'we believe adaptations are still important, but how to adapt remains to be explored'. The same section names the untried remedy: 'For systems that need to find the best parameter, downsized simulations using spatial sampling can be used [135, 136]'. Fig. 11 (p.13) quantifies the headroom - at the large cache size the P90 reduction peaks at S=1% while P10 wants a larger S, so no single static value is right everywhere. The failed adaptive variant is in the repo (S3FIFOd.c:37-40, two eviction-tracking ghost caches) as a directly comparable baseline.
addons.feasibility_rationale: One new ~500-LOC eviction module that reuses an existing sampler and the unmodified cachesim harness; ground truth for the comparison is shipped in result/cachesim_fifo/ and result/cachesim/. A 4-dataset sweep is tens of CPU-hours on 16 cores, comfortably inside budget. The main technical risk is shadow-cache noise at very small scale, which is itself part of the hypothesis under test.
addons.research_value_rationale: This is the paper's own explicitly named open problem, left open after the authors tried and failed with a different mechanism, and both outcomes teach something. If miniature simulation works, the 'static beats adaptive' thesis of 6.2 is overturned and S3-FIFO gains a principled tuning story. If it fails, the paper's claim that simplicity beats adaptation gets far stronger empirical backing than one hand-tuned variant provided. A SOSP/EuroSys reviewer would engage with either result.

scoop_check.details: Queries: 'miniature simulation shadow cache online parameter tuning S3-FIFO small queue size adaptive 2026'; 'adaptive queue size S3-FIFO improvement miss ratio curve spatial sampling 2025 2026'. The technique is Waldspurger et al., 'Cache Modeling and Optimization using Miniature Simulations', USENIX ATC '17 (https://www.usenix.org/conference/atc17/technical-sessions/presentation/waldspurger), which already auto-tunes the LIRS stack limit and 2Q queue sizes - and is reference [135] in this paper. No follow-up applying it to S3-FIFO was found; DynamicAdaptiveClimb (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.21235) does adaptive resizing for a different (Climb-family) policy. So the mechanism is known but its application to S3-FIFO is unclaimed; the project must frame the contribution as the empirical question, not the technique.

addons.name: Charging metadata against capacity: a fair re-evaluation
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that when per-algorithm metadata is charged against the cache's byte budget - LRU/ARC/2Q/LIRS paying 16 B of pointers per object, S3-FIFO paying 2 bits plus its ghost-queue entries - S3-FIFO's mean miss-ratio reduction over LRU grows by at least 3 percentage points on small-object KV workloads (Twitter, Meta KV) while changing by less than 0.5 points on 4 KB block workloads (MSR, Systor), and that S3-FIFO's ghost queue costs it ground at the 0.1%-footprint cache size.
addons.mechanism: The plumbing already exists: common_cache_params_t.consider_obj_metadata (include/libCacheSim/cache.h:33), a per-cache obj_md_size charged on every insert/evict (cache/cache.c:208,231,281), the --consider-obj-metadata CLI flag (bin/cachesim/cli_parser.c:146), and correct values for some baselines (LRU.c:66 = 8*2 bytes, ARCv0.c:111, LIRS.c:88, LeCaRv0.c:97). But S3FIFO.c:101 hard-codes cache->obj_md_size = 0 and ignores consider_obj_metadata entirely, and the ghost queue's storage is never charged. Work: (i) set S3-FIFO's obj_md_size honestly (the 2-bit counter rounded to its implementation byte, plus the amortised 4-byte-fingerprint + timestamp ghost cost the paper describes in 4.2); (ii) audit and fill in missing obj_md_size for TwoQ, SLRU, WTinyLFU, Clock, FIFO_Merge; (iii) re-run the Fig. 6 / Fig. 7 comparison on the open datasets with and without the flag and report the delta.
addons.motivating_evidence: Paper 5.1 (p.7): 'Moreover, we do not consider the metadata size in different algorithms, although S3-FIFO often requires fewer metadata than other algorithms' - the authors concede the comparison is biased and assert, without measuring, that the bias runs against themselves. 4.3 (p.7) gives the arithmetic (ghost ~0.09%, 2 bits <0.01%, saving 16 B/object vs LRU ~0.4%) but only for a 4 KB mean object; Table 1 (p.7) shows Twitter and Social-Network KV traces with mean objects an order of magnitude smaller, where 16 B/object is a several-percent capacity tax. 2.2 (pp.2-3) makes 'LRU requires two pointers per object' a headline motivation, so quantifying it is squarely on-thesis rather than a side quest.
addons.feasibility_rationale: Most of the work is filling in constants across ~8 files plus a careful accounting of the ghost queue's amortised cost; the harness, the CLI flag and the plotting scripts need no change. Evaluation is the same MSR/FIU/Systor/Twitter sweep as the reproduction, run twice. Low LOC, low compute, no new infrastructure.
addons.research_value_rationale: A reviewer would care: it turns a hand-waved footnote into a measured result and could either strengthen or partly deflate the headline margin, and it exposes a real accounting gap in the released simulator (S3FIFO.c:101). But it is a methodological correction rather than a new mechanism, and the expected direction is already stated by the authors, which caps the surprise value.

scoop_check.details: Query: 'cache eviction simulator metadata overhead fair comparison S3-FIFO LRU pointers charged cache capacity study'. Nothing found that re-evaluates the S3-FIFO trace corpus under a metadata-charged capacity budget. Related but different: Eytan et al., 'It's Time to Revisit LRU vs. FIFO', HotStorage '20 (https://www.usenix.org/system/files/hotstorage20_paper_eytan.pdf), which argues about LRU-vs-FIFO evaluation methodology but predates S3-FIFO and does not charge metadata against capacity.

addons.name: Write-amplification-aware main queue for DRAM+flash S3-FIFO
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that replacing S3-FIFO's physical main-queue reinsertion (which re-writes an object whenever its frequency bit is set) with an in-place DRAM-resident frequency update plus a segment-aligned eviction scan reduces flash write bytes by at least 25% at equal or lower miss ratio, on the Wikimedia and Tencent Photo CDN traces at the DRAM ratios of Figure 9 (0.1%, 1%, 10%).
addons.mechanism: flash.cpp:68-80 already shows that when S3-FIFO/QDLP's main cache is a Clock, write bytes are counted as n_byte_admit_to_main + n_byte_move_to_main + clock_params->n_byte_rewritten, i.e. reinsertion is a first-class, already-instrumented source of flash writes. Add a main-cache variant that (a) keeps the 2-bit counter in a DRAM-resident index rather than beside the data on flash, (b) at eviction scans a fixed-size window (a segment) of the flash FIFO tail and drops the coldest objects instead of rewriting the hot ones, (c) rewrites only when a whole segment is evicted, FIFO-merge style (FIFO_Merge.c is present as a reference implementation). Sweep segment size and compare (miss ratio, write bytes) Pareto fronts against the paper's FIFO / probabilistic / Flashield points.
addons.motivating_evidence: Paper 5.4 (p.11): 'Because the flash cache eviction algorithm is orthogonal to the admission policy, we used FIFO [14, 24, 102] in all experiments (including in S3-FIFO)' - an assumption asserted, never tested. 2.1 (p.2) argues flash lifetime is a first-class metric and that small random writes cause device-level write amplification; Algorithm 1 line 36 (p.6) makes reinsertion into M exactly such a write. Fig. 9 (p.11) shows the admission filter alone drops normalised write bytes from ~3x to well under 1x, so what remains of the write budget is dominated by the mechanism the paper pinned to FIFO. 4.3 (pp.6-7) hand-waves the cost ('the number of reinsertions is much smaller than the cache hits in practice') without measuring it.
addons.feasibility_rationale: Big head start: the flash harness, the write-byte accounting including n_byte_rewritten, and both traces (wiki_2019t, tencent_photo1, download URLs at doc/AE.md:283-284, both on the open PDL FTP) already exist. But it is a cross-cutting change - a new main-cache type that must cooperate with QDLP's byte accounting and with flash.cpp's per-algorithm branches - and if the team wants the Flashield comparison line, scripts/flashield/flashield.py is documented as taking 'more than one day to run' per configuration (doc/AE.md:309); budget for that or reuse the numbers pre-filled in scripts/plot_write_amp.py.
addons.research_value_rationale: It attacks the one place where the paper's simplification ('eviction is orthogonal to admission') is most likely to be false, in a regime - flash endurance - that the paper itself argues is economically important and that the production systems it cites (CacheLib large-object cache, Google Colossus, Memcached extstore, Apache Traffic Server) actually deploy. A positive result gives a deployable design; a negative result ('reinsertion writes are negligible once quick demotion is in place') is a genuinely useful confirmation of an unverified orthogonality claim.

scoop_check.details: Query: 'S3-FIFO flash cache admission write amplification follow-up reinsertion flash-friendly 2025 2026'. Closest work: CacheSack (ACM TOS 2023, https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3582014), Google's datacenter flash admission optimiser - same metric pair (miss ratio vs write bytes) but an admission-policy optimiser, and it predates S3-FIFO's flash section. Nothing found that measures or removes S3-FIFO's own main-queue reinsertion write cost.

risks: Disk vs corpus: the full 6594-trace / ~2 TB compressed dataset (doc/AE.md:44) does not fit in ~257 GB free. Every claim must be scoped to a named downloadable subset, and the write-up must be explicit that it re-tests 'across traces' robustness on 3-5 of 14 datasets, not all 14.

Proprietary data: CDN 1, CDN 2 and Social Network 1 (1711 of 6594 traces, 3 of the 14 rows of Fig. 7) are not on the PDL FTP and cannot be regenerated; add-on claims can only be validated on the open 12 datasets.

Figure 8 (throughput/scalability) is effectively out of reach: the prototype lives in a separate repo (README.md:45, doc/AE.md:227 -> Thesys-lab/cachelib-sosp23), CacheLib takes 'a few minutes up to one hour' to build with a large C++ dependency tree, doc/AE.md:219 asks for an Intel CPU (this machine is Zen 3), and 'bash turboboost.sh disable' (doc/AE.md:231) needs root. Do not promise any scalability number.

CMake version trap: libCacheSim/CMakeLists.txt:1 is cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.2); the system CMake 3.25.1 accepts it with a deprecation warning, but CMake 4.x from 'pip install cmake' rejects <3.5 outright.

Bugs/quirks in the reference implementation that must be pinned down before attributing any delta to a change: S3FIFO.c:290 is 'obj->S3FIFO.freq == 0;', a no-op comparison where an assignment was clearly intended (behaviour may be accidentally correct because the underlying FIFO insert zeroes the field); bin/cachesim/cache_init.h:98 makes 'fifo-reinsertion' unreachable as a distinct algorithm because the branch at l.89 catches it first. Establish a byte-for-byte baseline match against result/cachesim/ first.

Memory at high parallelism: --num-thread defaults to n_cores() (cli_parser.c:206) = 32 here, and doc/AE.md:46 warns that many algorithms x sizes in parallel multiplies DRAM use; uncapped runs on large traces will thrash into the 44 GiB swap on this shared machine.

Add-on 2 depends on sampling fidelity: at the paper's 0.1%-footprint 'small' cache size the real cache holds only thousands of objects, so 1/100-scale shadow instances would hold tens - possibly too noisy to rank. Mitigation: restrict the adaptive claim to the large cache size or use a coarser sample ratio and accept more overhead.

Crowded follow-up field: since 2023 this line has attracted SIEVE (NSDI '24, already vendored as eviction/Sieve.c), Mobius lock-free eviction (SIGMETRICS '25, https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3727136 - which is why no lock-free/ring-buffer add-on is proposed), 3L-Cache (FAST '25), a PVLDB lazy-promotion study (https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol19/p549-yang.pdf) and SCION. Re-run the scoop check at proposal time.

repo_facts.json red flags are benign, verified by reading the files: the multi_node hits are CloudLab/distComp references in distributedComputation/ and the acknowledgements; the docker hits are comments inside libCacheSim/dockerfile; the sudo hits are the apt convenience script and commented transparent-hugepage tuning. None is load-bearing for the simulator.
